s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial swelling and sinus pressure with nasal septum deviation and proptosis
salient_findings: Heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus with solid and cystic components
key_facts: Teenage girl presented with several months of sinus pressure and facial swelling
Several weeks of external deviation of her nasal septum
No significant past medical history
Left nasal mass noted on examination
Mild left-sided proptosis present
CT scan showed a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells
Displacement of inferior rectus without muscle invasion
Left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots involved
Bony changes showed remodeling and thinning
Biopsy showed spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells
Rare mitotic activity
No cytologic atypia

No significant past medical history
Left nasal mass noted on examination

CT scan showed a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells

Rare mitotic activity
No cytologic atypia

shortlist.label: Central Giant Cell Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of facial swelling, nasal septum deviation, and proptosis, with biopsy showing spindle cell process and multinucleated giant cells

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical and biopsy findings to Central Giant Cell Granuloma, but less common in this age group and location

shortlist.label: Ossifying Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain bony changes and remodeling, but less likely given biopsy results

shortlist.label: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Could cause nasal obstruction and facial swelling, but typically occurs in adolescent males and has distinct biopsy findings

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain bony changes and remodeling, but less likely given clinical presentation and biopsy results

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterogeneous mass in the maxillary sinus with significant multinucleated giant cells, rare mitotic activity, and no cytologic atypia, along with the patient's age and symptoms, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor of bone
rejected.why: Typically occurs in older patients and has more aggressive features

rejected.label: Ossifying Fibroma
rejected.why: Usually has a more solid and fibrous component, and the biopsy results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
rejected.why: Typically occurs in males and has a more vascular component, which is not mentioned in the biopsy results

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Does not typically present with a mass or multinucleated giant cells on biopsy
